decisions.quote:
Our application of his methods to more recent data shows that the results that
              Amihud identified in his analyses are time-dependent. We find that illiquidity
              appears to have been priced in the cross-section during the later period, but its
              relation to asset prices is much less strong than in the earlier period. The time-
              series results show that only unexpected illiquidity is related to index returns
              in the latter period whereas Amihud finds that both unexpected and expected
              illiquidity are related in the earlier period.
decisions.location: Independent parent reading of exact primary Methods/Discussion and original-specific context; raw contiguous extraction retained
decisions.reason: The author original-specific synthesis affirms later-period cross-sectional illiquidity pricing but explicitly finds only unexpected, not expected, illiquidity related to index returns, contrasting Amihud original both-component result. This named disagreement and agreement support mixed, beyond a mere weaker coefficient. Recovering the old-period numerical result cannot be transferred as an unqualified verdict about the new-period replication; the new illiquidity-measure comparison is a further extension.

prior_decisions.quote:
This paper replicates and extends the Amihud (2002) study that links
                      liquidity to asset pricing. Using the current version of the CRSP
                      dataset, we obtain essentially the same results that Amihud presents.
                      The same methods applied to more recent data show a much weaker
                      relation between liquidity and asset pricing.
prior_decisions.reason: The source combines original-period CRSP reconstruction with a separate newer-period sample. The first scalar outcome judgment addressed only the latter. The second/final type-and-axis scope review reached its ten-minute CLI limit with no JSON answer, so type and dependent outcome remain unverified; no third call.
